skill.name: repo-intake-and-plan
skill.description: Scans an AI repository before reproduction, extracts documented commands from README content, classifies likely inference, evaluation, and training paths, and recommends the smallest trustworthy next step.
skill.summary: Scan an AI repo and plan the smallest trustworthy reproduction path.
skill.author: lllllllama

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backtick parsing and a PowerShell language-label string. No evidence found of command execution, network access, prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration in the reviewed files.

static_findings.snippet: if lang and lang not in {"bash", "shell", "sh", "zsh", "powershell", "cmd"}:

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 13 defines a Python regular expression for Markdown fenced code blocks. It does not execute Ruby, shell commands, or backtick content.
The PowerShell token is only an allowed Markdown code-block language label during README parsing. The script does not invoke PowerShell or subprocess execution.
The backticks wrap file and directory names in prose documentation. This is Markdown formatting, not command execution or shell interpolation.

content.value_statement: AI reproduction work often stalls when commands and entry points are unclear. This skill scans repository evidence and returns a conservative reproduction plan.
actual_capabilities: Finds README files and common environment files in a target repository.
Extracts shell-like commands from Markdown code blocks and prompt-style lines.
Classifies command candidates as inference, evaluation, training, or other.
Labels commands as setup, asset, smoke, or run tasks.
Reports top-level structure details and missing-evidence warnings.
Recommends a small reproduction target based on documented evidence.
limitations: It does not install environments or run reproduction commands.
It depends on README content and common project files for evidence.
It cannot verify benchmark accuracy or runtime success.
It is a helper skill, not an end-to-end reproduction orchestrator.

use_cases.title: Initial Repo Triage
use_cases.description: Map a new AI repository before selecting setup, inference, evaluation, or training work.

use_cases.title: Reproduction Planning
use_cases.description: Identify the smallest documented command path that can support a trustworthy first result.

use_cases.title: Command Inventory Review
use_cases.description: Collect and classify documented commands before a larger agent starts environment setup.

prompt_templates.title: Scan a Repository
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a local repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this repository. Summarize the structure, README evidence, documented commands, and the smallest trustworthy reproduction target.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Command Candidates
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of documented command evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the README and common project files. Extract documented command candidates and classify each as setup, inference, evaluation, training, or other.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Inference First
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a low-cost first reproduction path.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this repository with inference as the priority. Identify the clearest documented demo path and list ambiguity that could affect execution.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reproduction Paths
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across multiple candidate workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a conservative reproduction plan from repository evidence. Compare inference, evaluation, and training candidates, then recommend the minimum credible target.

output_examples.input: Scan a model repository before starting reproduction.
output: README found with setup and usage sections.
Inference candidates are documented more clearly than training commands.
Recommended first target is a small demo or smoke run.
Risk noted: dataset and checkpoint requirements need confirmation.

output_examples.input: Classify documented commands from an AI project README.
output: Setup commands include package installation and environment activation.
Evaluation commands appear under benchmark documentation.
Training commands are present but require external assets.
Ambiguity remains around expected hardware and checkpoint paths.

output_examples.input: Recommend the smallest trustworthy reproduction target.
output: Choose the documented inference path before full evaluation.
Use README evidence as the source of truth.
Record missing assets, unclear configuration, and any inferred steps.

best_practices: Provide the target repository path and the desired reproduction priority.
Use README-backed commands before inferred entry points.
Review warnings and ambiguity before starting environment setup.
anti_patterns: Using the skill after execution has already started.
Treating inferred classifications as verified runtime results.
Expecting the skill to download assets or run long training jobs.

faq.question: Does this skill run repository commands?
faq.answer: No. It scans files, extracts documented command candidates, and recommends a plan.

faq.question: Which files does it prioritize?
faq.answer: It prioritizes README files, environment files, packaging files, Dockerfiles, and high-signal project directories.

faq.question: Can it classify training and evaluation commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It classifies documented candidates using section names and command text.

faq.question: Can it verify that a command succeeds?
faq.answer: No. Runtime verification must happen in a later setup or execution step.

faq.question: Is it useful for non-AI repositories?
faq.answer: It is optimized for AI and machine learning reproduction repositories.

faq.question: How should Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Use it early to map evidence and choose a conservative first reproduction target.
